evidence.text: TTLL11 is a tubulin polyglutamylase that adds glutamate side-chains to alpha-tubulin. This post-translational modification (polyglutamylation) modulates microtubule stability and motor protein recruitment. Encoded as Activation because INDRA lacks a Glutamylation statement type; the actual mechanism is enzymatic polyglutamylation. TTLL11 is inactivated (pseudogenised) in humans but functional in other great apes, making this a fossil interaction relevant to the meiotic drive hypothesis.

TTLL11 inactivation in humans may have been driven by meiotic drive: loss of polyglutamylation on spindle MTs could alter chromosome segregation fidelity or sperm motility, providing a selective advantage to the inactivating allele in the context of sex-chromosome conflict.

TTLL11 interacts with CCSAP (centriole, cilia and spindle-associated protein) for its localisation to spindle and ciliary microtubules. CCSAP recruits TTLL11 to its substrates, enabling site-specific polyglutamylation of the tubulin lattice. This interaction is conserved across mammals though TTLL11 is inactivated in humans.

TTLL5 glutamylates RPGR (retinitis pigmentosa GTPase regulator, X-linked at Xp11.4). RPGR requires polyglutamylation by TTLL5 for its function in ciliary trafficking in photoreceptors. Encoded as Activation because INDRA lacks a Glutamylation statement type; the actual mechanism is enzymatic polyglutamylation. Loss of TTLL5 function phenocopies RPGR mutations, causing retinal degeneration.
